In 2021, the U.S. age-adjusted drug overdose death rate was 32.4 per 100,000 population.
The highest rates were in West Virginia (90.9) and the District of Columbia (63.6)
The lowest state rates were those in Nebraska (11.4), South Dakota (12.6), and Iowa (15.3).
The figure is a map of the United States showing the age-adjusted drug overdose death rates

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted drug overdose death rates were calculated using the direct method and the 2000 U.S. Census Bureau standard population.
Drug overdose deaths were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision underlying cause-of-death codes X40–X44, X60–X64, X85, and Y10–Y14.
